defects: Crowd-scale identity still relies on the broad color arrangement; the twin optical lenses and manufactured headgear are too small to dominate at the 12-inch camera distance.
The production renderer receipt mixes this candidate with the moving scene and produces variable whole-scene workload metrics; it does not isolate the candidate or prove its per-citizen frame cost.
hard_fail_reasons: The current production capture measures the whole animated scene, and repeated v072/v073 detail results are mixed (15→20 FPS in run-001; 18→17 in run-002). The 29.3% asset triangle reduction is real, but runtime recovery is not established against v007.
At the 12-inch gameplay distance the Clockwork cues improve over v007 but remain too small for the highest role-recognition threshold in a 50-citizen scene.
incumbent_comparison: v073 preserves v072’s anatomy, Clockwork helmet, paired goggles, fitted workwear, and rear pressure pack while reducing the generated asset from 90,418 to 63,914 triangles (29.3%). The latest production images show no obvious faceting or loss of the paired optics, garment layers, or rear equipment. It remains a challenger: the 12-inch citizen is still small in the 50-citizen scene, and repeated whole-scene detail captures do not establish a reliable runtime improvement over v072 or v007. Keep v007 as the incumbent.
likely_causes: The camera places a half-inch figure among 50 active citizens, making the head-mounted optical detail occupy only a small number of pixels.

Only one selected candidate replaces the regular crowd asset in the whole-scene capture, and the scene state changes between runs; aggregate draw calls/primitives/FPS therefore obscure per-asset cost.
next_action_hypothesis: Keep v007 as incumbent and v073 as challenger. First add a controlled Art Factory performance comparison that renders the same candidate as the same 50-citizen workload from a fixed camera after warm-up, reporting repeated frame-time percentiles and candidate triangle/material counts; do not infer performance from the changing whole-scene receipt. Then, if the budget still requires it, test a distance-aware lower-detail citizen representation while preserving the detailed close asset, rig, five pivots, package bounds, gameplay equipment, and collision/navigation/selection contracts. Separately improve 12-inch Clockwork role recognition through broad, physically plausible silhouette/material cues, not scattered tiny hardware.

observations.art_direction_fit: The render now reads as a believable miniature pressure-equipped Clockwork worker from the front and back, rather than a generic green human.
observations.close_up_quality: The latest matched two-inch render preserves distinct brass-rimmed teal lenses, the formed helmet shell, layered workwear, and twin rear reservoirs. The lower triangle count causes no obvious faceting in the production capture; the production-owned tool still obscures part of the lower front.
observations.gameplay_readability: The 12-inch image retains a recognizable helmet, bright goggles, warm chest yoke, blue-green workcoat, and rear pressure kit. At crowd scale, the character remains small and the paired optics cannot carry role identity by themselves.
observations.geometric_detail: The fitted MPFB anatomy and 53-bone rig remain unchanged. Authored helmet hardware, bands, tubes, tanks, boots, and curves use fewer segments; validation records 63,914 triangles versus 90,418 in v072, with exact bounds and the same eight meshes/18 surfaces.
observations.material_realism: Teal-blue cloth, warm canvas, dark leather, brass, dark steel, glass, and skin remain differentiated under production lighting.
observations.proportion: The reservoirs and optics are larger, but remain within exact package bounds and are proportionate to miniature pressure-worker equipment.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot validates exact 0.26 x 0.50 x 0.21 inch bounds and all five required pivots.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The front 3/4 reads as a Clockwork worker with twin glass optics, metal helmet, warm canvas workwear, and a tool harness. The back 3/4 shows a fitted shoulder yoke and twin pressure reservoirs, so role identity no longer depends solely on the face.
observations.silhouette_quality: The broad shoulder yoke and paired rear tanks add a useful role silhouette from the back; the front is defined by the enlarged paired optics and helmet brow.
observations.surface_variation: The broad canvas areas separate clearly from the deep coat and metal/glass equipment in the front and back views.
observations.technical_integration: Godot validation passes with exact 0.26 × 0.50 × 0.21 inch bounds, eight meshes, 18 surfaces, and the preserved 53-bone rig/five pivots. Generated triangles fell 29.3% from v072 (90,418 to 63,914). Whole-scene detail receipts are not stable enough to show a runtime recovery: run-001 is v072 15 FPS/v073 20 FPS, while run-002 is v072 18/v073 17; v007 also varied from 45 FPS in run-005 to 25 in run-006. Whole-scene primitive counts vary independently of the candidate’s triangle reduction, so this is not a controlled per-citizen performance measurement.

close_inspection.evidence: The paired lenses, bridge, brow, temple hardware, seams, canvas yoke, and pressure vessels read clearly in the matched three-quarter, profile, and detail renders.

edge_treatment.evidence: Helmet brow, lens rings, apron/yoke hems, cuffs, and pack crossbars have modeled finished edges.

hardware.evidence: Twin rims, central hinge, buckles, gauge, retaining bands, ferrules, and twin reservoirs are visible at close range.

joins.evidence: The optics attach through a structural bridge/brow, the rear yoke follows the body, and straps join it to the pressure frame.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: The face cage, helmet supports, fitted rear yoke, reservoir straps, gauge, and pack rails form functional assemblies.

material_response.evidence: Cloth, canvas, leather, brass, steel, glass, and skin respond differently to production lighting.

surface_variation.evidence: Warm canvas, deep blue-green cloth, dark leather, metal, and teal glass stay visually separated.

thickness.evidence: Helmet, optical barrels, canvas panels, harness, pressure tanks, and boots have actual thickness.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: Anatomical proportions, fitted cloth and canvas, leather harness, paired optical glass, machined helmet hardware, and a connected pressure pack form a believable miniature industrial worker.

photo_character.evidence: The Citizen ArtBrief has no photographic reference.
